chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ghiyāth, from Jaʿfar, from his father عليه السلام, who said:

A man should not perform salat (prayer) with his buttons undone when he is not wearing an izar. The meaning in these two reports is a degree of reprehensibility, not prohibition; that is indicated by this.

key_terms.الْكَرَاهِيَةِ: reprehensibility or dislikedness in legal context
key_terms.مَحْلُولَ الْأَزْرَارِ: with the buttons undone or loosened

ai.seo_question: Is it forbidden or merely disliked to pray with one's garment unbuttoned when not wearing an izar?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling on performing salat (prayer) with one's garment unfastened when no izar is being worn. It indicates that the matter is understood as karahah (reprehensibility) rather than outright prohibition, placing it within the etiquettes and legal rulings of prayer.
